title: fix(plugin-audit): consume the engine's bound `ctx.previous` and record one normalised view on both sides of the diff (#6656)
body:
Fixes #6656

Implements the maintainer's **Option A+** ruling (2026-08-09, comment 5230191737). Both halves are here; the first alone was the ruled-out Option A.

## Half 1 — the plugin's own pre-image read is retired

`captureBefore` issued a `ql.findOne` on `beforeUpdate` / `beforeDelete` and stashed the row on `ctx.__previous`, because `HookContext.previous` was "officially typed but not always populated by the engine itself". That justification has expired, and it was **re-verified in code on this branch point** rather than taken from the card. The anchors moved since #5846 recorded them, so they are restated:

| face | dispatch | `previous` bound | demand gate |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| single-id update | `engine.ts:7012` | `:7010` | `:6992` `wantsPriorRecord` |
| single-id delete | `:7899` | `:7896`/`:7897` (`readPreImage` → `bindPreImage`) | `:7857` `wantsPreImage` |
| predicate update | `:7084` `dispatchPerRowBeforeHooks` | `:1825` per row | `:7067` |
| predicate delete | `:7962` `dispatchPerRowBeforeHooks` | `:1825` per row | `:7949` |

Each demand gate is the **same predicate** as its dispatch gate, so no path exists on which the hook runs unbound. One fact worth adding to the card's record: `buildPerRowAfterContexts` (`:1746`) also binds `previous` on every per-row `afterUpdate` / `afterDelete` context — which is the face `writeAudit` actually runs on, so the predicate path was already falling through to `previous` while the single-id path used the stash. That is precisely the "last inconsistent island" the decision card described.

Measured with a counting driver (`driver.findOne` on the audited object, per write):

| write | before | after |
|:--|--:|--:|
| single-id `update()` | 2 | 1 |
| single-id `delete()` | 2 | 1 |
| predicate `update()`, 3 matched rows | 3 | 0 |
| predicate `delete()`, 3 matched rows | 3 | 0 |

The predicate column was pure waste: #5574 binds `input.id` on every per-row *before* context, defeating the handler's own `if (!id) return` bulk guard, so it read every matched row and discarded every result. The engine's own matched-row read is untouched and still serves both phases, so the ledger is unchanged.

Retired outright rather than left as a no-op registration: a hook whose only remaining effect is holding a demand gate open is exactly what `sys_fetch_previous_delete` had become when #5929 removed it from objectql's own plugin. The `afterInsert` / `afterUpdate` / `afterDelete` registrations stay, and they are what hold the gates open on their after-hook term.

## Half 2 — one view on both sides of the diff

Half 1 makes both sides same-**source**. Half 2 gives them one **view**, so the surface levels upward instead of down to raw store contents. New `ledgerView(objectName, record, { dropComputed })`, non-mutating (`ctx.result` is the record the caller receives, and some drivers hand out live store references).

**Limb 1 — credential fields, masked on both sides.** `SECRET_MASK` and `collectMaskedReadFields` are imported from `@objectstack/objectql/core` rather than re-typed, so this cannot drift from the engine's own read mask by a character. Change detection still runs on the **raw** values and only the recorded values are masked — otherwise "fix the phantom rows" would have silently deleted the audit trail of every secret rotation. There is a pin for exactly that.

**Limb 2 — virtual fields dropped from full snapshots.** `ctx.result` carries hydrated formulas (#5504); the raw pre-image structurally cannot, so create `new_value` would describe a field delete `old_value` could never carry.

**File-reference fields need no limb, and that is a measurement rather than an omission.** They are named in the ruling because today's `before` carries the resolved `{ id, name, size, url }` object against a raw id on the `after` side. Once the pre-image is the engine's, both sides hold the stored id token and agree by construction. An "if it looks resolved, take `.id`" limb would be consumer-side tolerance for a producer that no longer exists (PD #12), and could never be shown to go red.

### A fourth field class the card did not name

The `password` type. ADR-0100 stores it **plaintext at rest** and masks it only on read, so the pre-existing leak was worse than the `secret:` ref the ruling names — the cleartext was landing in `sys_audit_log.new_value` on every create and update, and in the `sys_activity` summary rendered verbatim in the record feed. `collectMaskedReadFields` covers it, so the same limb closes it. Measured before the fix:

```
CREATE new_value: {"api_key":"secret:sec_98uiuw","login_pw":"hunter2", ...}
```

## Behaviour changes, stated plainly

- Single-id delete `old_value` keeps `••••••••` for credential fields — **byte-identical**, the compliance face the ruling protects. The row as a whole is not byte-identical: a file field now records its stored id rather than the resolved object, and formula values are gone. Both narrow single-id delete to what bulk delete already did.
- An object whose label field is a formula falls back to the record id in the `sys_activity` label on delete, for the same reason. Bulk delete already behaved this way.
- A secret rotation now records `{"api_key":"••••••••"}` on both sides — "it changed", without saying to what.

## Reverse verification

Direction predicted in writing **before** running each mutation.

| mutation | predicted | measured |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **R1** restore `captureBefore` + its two registrations | 4 read-count pins red (2/2/3/3) | ✅ exactly those deltas — **and 6 more**, see below |
| **R2** delete the mask limb | credential pins red | ✅ 6 red; delete `old_value` shows `secret:…` and `hunter2` |
| **R3a** delete the snapshot limb | snapshot pin red | ✅ 1 red (`upper_title` survives) |
| **R3b** widen the limb back to `COMPUTED_FIELD_TYPES` | not predicted — this mutation exists *because of* what R3a found | ✅ 1 red (`ticket_no` lost) |
| **R4** file-reference | **no limb to delete**, so nothing of mine can turn a file-specific guard red | ✅ confirmed: it goes red under R1 only |

**Honest deltas.**

1. **R1 turned 10 tests red, not 4.** The phantom-row and credential-rotation pins went red too, because with `__previous` restored the diff regains its extra keys and those cases assert the diff *exactly*. So half 1 and half 2 are not pinned by disjoint sets — the phantom-row cases bite on half 1. Stronger than predicted, and worth knowing before anyone reads a single red as localised.

2. **R3a exposed an over-reach in my own limb, and changed the implementation.** It could only be made red on the *create* face; chasing why showed the delete face could never bite, because the limb keyed off `COMPUTED_FIELD_TYPES` and of that set only `formula` is virtual. `autonumber` is seeded at insert and `summary` is written by `recomputeSummaries` — both are stored columns, present and equal on both sides, and dropping them was deleting the record's human-facing number and its roll-up values from the ledger to fix an asymmetry they never had. Narrowed to a new `VIRTUAL_FIELD_TYPES`, documented against the wider set so a later reader does not unify them, and now pinned in **both** directions (R3a and R3b).

3. **Guards that correctly stayed green, reported as results rather than tidied away.** "An unset credential stays `null`" survives R2 — without masking a null stays null anyway. It guards the opposite mutation (masking unconditionally), which is the right job for it.

## Probe hygiene

The counting driver in the new test file returns **deep copies** on every read, unlike the one in `audit-hook-object-scope.test.ts`. A driver handing back live store references lets the engine's read-path `maskSecretFields` rewrite the store in place, after which the two views this file exists to distinguish look identical and every assertion passes for the wrong reason. That contamination produced the *opposite* conclusion on the first investigation of this card before it was caught; the file says so where the driver is defined.

## Tests and gates

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit test` — **137 passed / 9 files** (was 122; +15).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit typecheck` — clean.
- `pnpm lint` (repo-wide, as the ESLint job runs it) — clean.
- All 33 family gates in the ESLint job run individually — all PASS, including `check:kernel-hook-pairs` (this PR removes a before/after pair), `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:published-files`.

Existing tests updated rather than worked around:
- 18 `__previous` fixtures in `audit-writers.test.ts` **re-spelled** to `previous` — they used the plugin's private stash, never a contract.
- Two read-count cases had `crm_lead` as a *control that still paid* the read. The read is retired for every object now, so the control joins the assertion instead of opposing it — a strictly larger surface, since restoring `captureBefore` now turns them red on `crm_lead` where the old version required that read.
- `audit-hook-object-scope.test.ts` — `beforeUpdate`/`beforeDelete` gates now assert `false` for a business object, with the after-terms asserted alongside so the pair can never quietly come to mean "audit stopped seeing the prior row". `AUDIT_WRITER_EVENTS` five → three; #5860's `excludeObjects` property is unchanged and still measured on every surviving registration.

## Scope

`packages/plugins/plugin-audit` only. `packages/objectql` untouched (`sys_fetch_previous_delete` is #5929, engine-core lane); #5860's registration-face work not reopened; `content/docs/releases/` untouched. No behaviour is keyed off `ctx.input.options.multi` — the contract value is consumed unconditionally, per the ruling's boundary and #4434 / #4550.

`@objectstack/objectql` moves from `devDependencies` to `dependencies` for the two imported contract symbols. No cycle (objectql does not depend on plugin-audit), and `plugin-sharing` already takes the same runtime dependency.

Downstream: **#6965** is subsumed by this PR — commented there for triage rather than closed from here. **#6966** is untouched and remains cross-lane.
